name: batch statistics and affine
input: (2,3) matrix with distinct scales and shifts
test:
import torch
x = torch.tensor([[1., 3., 8.], [-4., 2., 5.]])
gamma = torch.tensor([2., -1., 0.5]); beta = torch.tensor([1., 3., -2.])

y = batch_norm(x, gamma, beta)
expected = torch.nn.functional.batch_norm(x, None, None, gamma, beta, training=True, eps=1e-5)
assert y.shape == x.shape and y.dtype == x.dtype
assert torch.allclose(y, expected, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
print('ok')

name: constant feature and singleton batch
input: constant feature, N=1, D=1, and eps=0.25

name: float64 and unchanged inputs
test:
import torch
x = torch.tensor([[1., 4., -2.], [0., 2., 8.]], dtype=torch.float64).T
gamma = torch.tensor([2., -1.], dtype=x.dtype); beta = torch.tensor([1., 3.], dtype=x.dtype)
saved = [v.clone() for v in (x, gamma, beta)]
y = batch_norm(x, gamma, beta, eps=0.02)
expected = torch.nn.functional.batch_norm(x, None, None, gamma, beta, training=True, eps=0.02)
assert y.shape == x.shape and y.dtype == x.dtype
assert torch.allclose(y, expected, atol=1e-9, rtol=1e-7)
for v, old in zip((x, gamma, beta), saved):
    assert torch.equal(v, old)
print('ok')
